**`THINGS-TO-DO.md` is incomplete:** it leaves out 35 of the 68 page-audit items labelled P1 (high priority), including all of import review. I added them here.

I only rechecked the three step 1 fixes and the missing root error pages in the code, and all are still open. Everything else comes from the reports, and `main` has no newer commits.

## 1. Fix first: access and safety
- **Sign out:** there's no way to sign out anywhere in the app.
- **Expired sessions:** signed-out users get an error instead of the login page, and should return to the page they wanted after signing in.
- **AI prompts in links:** opening a `?start=` link sends a paid AI prompt with no click. This really happened during the Claude audit, and a tab link can trigger it too.

## 2. Money accuracy and trust
- **Partial totals:** "Net worth EUR 500" can come from just 1 of 7 accounts. Show the coverage next to the number, with a guided way to fix balances.
- **Expense proposals:** near-identical cards can record the same purchase several times, and they default to creating a new Cash account.
- **Hidden side effects:**
  - The "future rule" box is ticked by default in Organization.
  - Approving a category can also allow unrelated edits.
  - Adding your own IBAN reclassifies existing transactions without saying so.
- **Recurring:** ALDI is offered as weekly, biweekly and monthly from only 3 payments each. Show one row per merchant and rank real bills first.
- **Import review:** show the interpreted transaction and duplicate choice before accepting, and let people undo accepted or rejected rows.
- **Investigations:** label unequal-period comparisons and show exclusions beside totals.
- **Other risks:**
  - Currency-linked account choices don't update when the currency changes in Wealth.
  - Organization mixes financial-review entries with safe organizing work.
  - A failed "Reset all data" can hide that part of it already ran.

## 3. Crashes, errors and recovery
- **Bad links:** add root not-found and error pages. Invalid URLs currently crash the page or show raw database and Zod errors.
- **Failed loads:** these currently look like empty data or "all done" on Home, Plan, Currency, Recurring, Activity and Notifications.

- **Modal:** the panel takes over and the page behind it is locked. Tab stays inside the panel, and Escape closes it and returns you to the button you opened it from.
- **Non-modal:** the panel sits beside the page, so you can keep clicking and reading the page while it's open.

On a phone the panel fills the screen, so you can't use the page behind it anyway, and it should act as a modal. On desktop there's room for both, so it should stay non-modal. Today Escape only works if your focus is already inside the panel (`components/ai-panel-dialog.tsx:131`), which is why it sometimes appears to do nothing.

My recommendation is modal on phone and non-modal on desktop, with Escape closing it on both.

## Implementation plan
I'll make one commit per fix on this branch and add a test for each behaviour change. I'll run the relevant tests after each step, and `npm test`, `npm run lint` and `npm run build` before finishing.

1. **Repair the test setup:** find out why the database and auth setup makes 30 browser tests fail, then fix it and update the outdated date test. This gives me a baseline to test against.
2. **Access and safety:**
   - **Expired sessions:** `proxy.ts` sends signed-out page requests to `/login?next=<path>`. Only paths inside the app are allowed as `next`, and the login, reset, legal and API routes stay as they are.
   - **Sign out:** add it to Settings, the phone More menu and the command palette.
   - **AI prompts in links:** remove `?start=` auto-send, so a prompt only goes out after someone presses a button.
3. **Money accuracy:**
   - **Totals:** show coverage on every partial total, such as "EUR 500 from 1 of 7 accounts", with a link to fix balances.
   - **Forecast:** run it from usable accounts and show coverage.
   - **Proposals:** group repeats and apply the default account rules you approved, and any new account is named on the button.
   - **Rules and recurring:** make future rules opt-in, and show one recurring row per merchant.
   - **Remaining risks:** fix import review, Investigations labels, the Wealth currency choices, the IBAN warning and reset failures.
4. **Errors and recovery:**
   - **Bad links:** add root not-found and error pages, and validate URL parameters.
   - **Failed loads:** show a clear error with Retry instead of an empty state.

Code review only. Do not edit files, commit, push, or comment on GitHub. An Opus agent implements the fixes from your findings.

**Repo:** Moneo, a Next.js 16 / React 19 / Supabase personal-finance app. Read AGENTS.md first. For Next behaviour, check `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` rather than memory. Your worktree is at commit 16568143.

**Scope:** `git diff 28b90ac7..HEAD` (about 89 commits, not yet pushed). 28b90ac7 is the current head of PR #140, "Fix user-testing audit findings across access, money accuracy, recovery and layout". Read surrounding code where the diff depends on it. Look outside the range only to confirm a defect in it.

**What the commits are meant to do:** fix findings from a user-testing audit. The source reports are git-ignored, so read them from the main checkout: `C:/Users/mgsuk/.t3/worktrees/Moneo/t3-7d9fff38/.qa/user-testing` (read only that directory there, and do not read `.env` anywhere). Recent work includes individual import-row accept/reject undo with history and dependency refusal (migration 202611040004), a null-relation crash fix on rejected import rows, and changes to the SQL migration test harness (`supabase/tests/migrations.mjs`, `migration-replay.mjs`, `scripts/acceptance.mjs`).

**Look for, in priority order:**
1. Money and data correctness: integer minor units, explicit currency, preserved source records, correction history and undo semantics, partial totals shown as complete.
2. Security: RLS and workspace isolation, SECURITY DEFINER functions, auth and redirect handling, input validation (Zod is the pattern), secrets or personal data in logs or committed files.
3. Migrations: rewriting applied migrations, `lib/schema.ts` drift, ordering, fresh versus upgrade differences. 202611040001 to 202611040004 are already applied to the QA database, so a fix must be a new migration.
4. User-visible bugs: broken flows, error and loading states, regressions against the audit findings, accessibility of changed UI.
5. Tests that pass without proving anything, such as weakened assertions or swallowed errors.
6. Needless complexity, only where it is a real maintenance risk.

**Constraints:**
- Do not run database gates, `supabase/tests/migrations.mjs`, Playwright, or anything that connects to a database. Another agent is running serialized DB gates against the shared QA database. Static reading plus DB-free unit tests are fine.
- Known and out of scope: 9 uncommitted SQL fixture edits are being finished separately, and the fresh SQL gate currently fails on `planning-history.sql` for that work. Real bank, email, paid provider, voice and deployed behaviour are unverified. Older import decisions have no undo receipts.

**Report:** findings most severe first. For each give severity (P0 to P3), `file:line`, the defect in one sentence, a concrete failure scenario (input or state leading to the wrong result), and the smallest fix. Only report what you verified by reading the code, and mark anything uncertain as such. Say which areas you covered and which you did not get to. If you find nothing serious, say so plainly rather than padding the list.

Code review only. Do not edit files, commit, push, or comment on GitHub. An Opus agent implements fixes from your findings.

**Repo:** Moneo, a Next.js 16 / React 19 / Supabase personal-finance app. Read AGENTS.md first. For Next behaviour, check `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` rather than memory.

**Scope:** `git diff 28b90ac7..HEAD`, limited to `app/` excluding `app/api/` and `app/money/`, plus `components/` and `e2e/`. A separate reviewer covers `lib/`, `app/api/`, `app/money/`, auth routes and SQL. Read surrounding code where the diff depends on it.

**Finish every path in scope before reporting.** An earlier review of this range stopped partway. Start with `git diff --stat 28b90ac7..HEAD -- app components e2e` and work through the list. At the end, name any file you did not read.

**Context:** the commits fix findings from a user-testing audit. Source reports are git-ignored, so read them from `C:/Users/mgsuk/.t3/worktrees/Moneo/t3-7d9fff38/.qa/user-testing` (only that directory there; do not read `.env` anywhere).

Decisions already made, so do not report these as defects:
- The AI panel is modal on phone and non-modal on desktop, with Escape closing it on both.
- Home widgets snap to the nearest slot, the desktop grid packs gaps, and widgets can be dragged by the card header or the grip.

**Look for, in priority order:**
1. User-visible bugs and regressions: broken flows, Home drag and drop, sign out, AI panel focus and Escape, plan and investigation screens.
2. Recovery: failed loads shown as empty data or "all done", forms losing typed input or errors not shown inline, root error and not-found pages, invalid URL params.
3. Trust in numbers shown: partial totals without coverage, unequal-period comparisons unlabelled, exclusions hidden, side effects not named on the button, currency choices out of sync.
4. Accessibility and layout of changed UI: labels, focus order, phone width, hydration mismatches, server/client boundary mistakes.
5. E2E specs that pass without proving anything: weakened assertions, swallowed errors, conditional skips, timing sleeps hiding real bugs.

**Constraints:** do not run the app, Playwright, database gates, or anything that connects to a database, because another agent is running serialized gates on the shared QA database. Static reading and DB-free unit tests are fine.

**Known, do not re-report:** real bank, email, paid provider, voice, screen reader and deployed behaviour are unverified. Older import decisions have no undo receipts.

**Report:** findings most severe first. For each give severity (P0 to P3), `file:line`, the defect in one sentence, a concrete failure scenario, and the smallest fix. Only report what you verified by reading the code, and mark anything uncertain. If nothing serious turns up, say so plainly.

content.text:
Sol's first review came back partial: one finding, and only part of the 189 changed files covered. I started two more Sol reviews for the rest:

- [Money, auth and schema](<t3-thread://v2/88042f69-c439-49f6-a4b9-1fb5180f2502/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A736c3475-3152-4638-8395-8b1173bef9e5%3Adelegate-task%3A80107a37-7a0b-461c-9b80-156f28311255>)
- [UI, recovery and E2E](<t3-thread://v2/88042f69-c439-49f6-a4b9-1fb5180f2502/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A736c3475-3152-4638-8395-8b1173bef9e5%3Adelegate-task%3A5bccfe60-adda-4a03-928f-8c12feeeaba1>)

**The finding is real, but Sol's suggested fix wouldn't work.** Sol found that if you correct an accepted import row's transaction and then undo the correction, the row still can't be reopened, even though the error tells you to undo the correction. Only checking for active corrections wouldn't fix this, for two reasons:
- **Version check:** undoing a correction bumps the transaction's version, so the snapshot comparison (`202611040004_import_row_decision_undo.sql:62`) refuses first.
- **Delete guard:** `202610010050_preserve_linked_sources.sql:8` deliberately blocks deleting any transaction with correction history, undone or not.

**Planned fix:** keep that guard, because AGENTS.md says correction history must be preserved. A new migration will check for correction history first and replace the misleading message with an accurate one: this row can't be reopened because its correction history is kept, so change it in Transactions instead. A SQL test will cover the correct-then-undo case.

The [Opus agent](<t3-thread://v2/88042f69-c439-49f6-a4b9-1fb5180f2502/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3Aad1b6865-07da-47b3-80c7-9128b36c5ae7%3Adelegate-task%3A0b8664e4-e71b-4e86-b9d7-345a06a74f90>) is still working on the SQL fixtures and migration gate. Once it and both reviews finish, all the fixes go in together, then acceptance runs and PR #140 gets updated.
